title: How a Car Allowance Salary Package Affects Your Hourly to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay including a car allowance salary package. Understand award rates, casual loading, super, and tax for 2026-27.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52; a car allowance salary package may be included in an annualised wage arrangement.

faqs.q: What is a car allowance salary package?
faqs.a: A car allowance salary package is an arrangement where your employer pays you a fixed annual amount that includes a car allowance, often as part of an annualised wage under an award or enterprise agreement. The allowance covers vehicle-related costs and is included in your regular pay rather than reimbursed separately. Under Fair Work rules, the total annualised wage must not be less than what you would have earned from all award entitlements (including the car allowance) for the work performed.

faqs.q: How does a car allowance affect my hourly to annual conversion?
faqs.a: When you have a car allowance salary package, your annual pay already includes the allowance. To compare with an hourly rate, divide your total annual salary (including the allowance) by (hours per week × 52). For a standard 38-hour week, that's 1,976 hours. If your package is expressed as an hourly rate plus a car allowance, add the allowance to your base hourly rate before multiplying. Remember that the car allowance may be subject to fringe benefits tax if not structured correctly – check with the Australian Taxation Office.

faqs.q: Is a car allowance salary package the same as being paid a salary under a contract?
faqs.a: No. A car allowance salary package is typically part of an annualised wage arrangement under an award or enterprise agreement, which must follow specific rules about record-keeping and annual reconciliation. A salary under an employment contract may offset award entitlements, but it still must meet the National Minimum Wage and National Employment Standards. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that annualised wages have their own rules and must be reviewed every 12 months to ensure the employee received at least the award minimum.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia

When you’re offered a job or negotiating a pay rise, you often see an hourly rate. But to compare offers or plan your budget, you need to convert that hourly rate to an annual figure. The basic formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This article assumes a standard full-time week of 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman for the National Minimum Wage. If you work part-time or casual, adjust the hours accordingly.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. For a 38-hour week, that’s $1,004.90 per week, or $52,254.80 per year (before tax and super). If you’re casual, you get a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour, or $65,318.50 per year. These figures come from the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) and the on-site reference.

### The Fortnightly View

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For the minimum wage example: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight. This can help you match your pay cycle to your budget.

## What About a Car Allowance Salary Package?

A **car allowance salary package** is a common way employers provide a vehicle benefit. Instead of reimbursing fuel and maintenance separately, they include a fixed amount in your annualised wage. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that annualised wages can cover entitlements like minimum pay rates, penalties, overtime, allowances, and annual leave loading. A car allowance is one such allowance.

When you have a car allowance salary package, your annual pay already includes that allowance. To convert your total package to an equivalent hourly rate, divide the annual amount by (hours per week × 52). For a 38-hour week, that’s 1,976 hours. If your package is $70,000 including a $5,000 car allowance, your effective hourly rate is $70,000 ÷ 1,976 ≈ $35.43 per hour.

### Important Rules for Annualised Wages

Employers using annualised wages must follow award rules. The Fair Work Ombudsman states that the annualised wage must not be less than what the employee would have received under the award for the work performed. Awards also set a maximum number of penalty rate or overtime hours before extra payment is due. Employers must review the arrangement every 12 months and pay any shortfall.

If your car allowance salary package is part of a salary under an employment contract (not an award annualised wage), the employer can offset above-award payments against award entitlements, but they still must meet the National Minimum Wage and National Employment Standards. The guide notes that allowances are extra payments for tasks, situations, and work-related costs.

## Distinguishing Pay Types

It’s crucial to know which pay system applies to you:

- **National Minimum Wage**: $26.44/hour for award/agreement-free employees. This is the legal floor.
- **Award rates**: Most industries have modern awards that set higher minimums for specific roles. Use the [pay guides](/blog) to find yours.
- **Casual loading**: Casual employees get an extra 25% on top of the base rate (e.g., $33.05/hour for minimum wage). Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into the calculator – use the base rate and check the casual loading box.
- **Superannuation**: Your employer must pay super guarantee of 12% of your ordinary earnings on top of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026-27). So if your annual gross is $70,000, your super contribution is $8,400, paid separately.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office’s 2026-27 resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 + 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 + 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 + 45% of excess over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). The on-site reference uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed. For a detailed estimate, use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool.

### Example: Minimum Wage Employee

- Hourly: $26.44
- Weekly (38h): $1,004.90
- Annual gross: $52,254.80
- Super (12%): $6,270.58 (paid on top)
- Tax (approx): $5,086 (using 2026-27 rates, ignoring Medicare levy for simplicity)
- Annual take-home: ~$47,169

## The Role of Salary Packaging

A **car allowance salary package** is a form of salary packaging. The Australian Taxation Office has specific rules about what counts as a fringe benefit. If your car allowance is structured as a salary sacrifice arrangement, it may reduce your taxable income but could incur fringe benefits tax. Always check with a tax professional. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page has more details.

## Common Questions

### How do I know if my car allowance is included in my annualised wage?

Your employment contract or award should specify which entitlements are covered. The Fair Work Ombudsman requires employers to provide a written agreement that includes the annualised wage amount, which entitlements are included, how it was calculated, and the maximum penalty/overtime hours without extra payment.

### Can my employer change my car allowance salary package mid-year?

Generally, no. Annualised wage arrangements are reviewed every 12 months. If your employment ends before the year is up, the employer must reconcile the payments and pay any shortfall.

### Does a car allowance affect my super?

Yes. Super guarantee is calculated on ordinary earnings, which includes allowances like a car allowance if it’s part of your regular pay. However, if the car allowance is a reimbursement of expenses, it may not count. Check with the Australian Taxation Office.

## Final Tips

- Always use the base hourly rate (without casual loading) in the [timesheet](/).
- For a car allowance salary package, add the allowance to your base rate before multiplying by hours.
- Remember that super is paid on top of your gross pay, not deducted from it.
- Use the [reference tables](/data) for award rates and tax brackets.

This article provides an estimate only. Your actual pay depends on your award, agreement, and personal circumstances. Always consult the Fair Work Ombudsman, Australian Taxation Office, or a qualified advisor for your specific situation.
